newKeyTerms.definition: The position that we cannot know whether God exists or what God is like. Feser argues that confining God-talk to univocal and equivocal terms would force us into agnosticism (or even atheism). Adjective/noun: “agnostic.”
newKeyTerms.example: Someone who says “God, if there is one, is so beyond us that nothing we say about him means anything” has slid into agnosticism.
newKeyTerms.origin: Coined by T. H. Huxley (1869) from Greek *a-* (“without”) + *gnosis* (“knowledge”).
newKeyTerms.confuseWith: Apophatic theology, which denies limitations of God while still affirming that he exists and causes the world.

newKeyTerms.definition: The view that God created the world but does not continually sustain or act in it, like a watchmaker who winds the watch and walks away. Adjective/noun: “deist,” “deistic.”
newKeyTerms.example: Picturing God as the one who lit the Big Bang’s fuse and then left.
newKeyTerms.confuseWith: Classical theism, on which God causes the existence of things at every moment (the hierarchical causation of chapters 1–5).
